title: Microsoft to Deploy 1 Million Maia 300 AI Chips Next Year for Primary Inference
summary:
Microsoft will make its in house Maia AI chips the primary system for running inference across all its services and products, including Copilot. The company intends to scale its Maia family to multi GW deployments starting in 2027, with reports from Reuters indicating plans to deploy more than 1 million Maia 300 accelerators next year. This transition to proprietary silicon aims to reduce dependence on Nvidia and AMD while optimizing data center margins by moving the majority of internal compute consumption to homegrown hardware.

The newly unveiled Maia 300 accelerator is manufactured by TSMC on a 2nm process and features eight HBM4 memory stacks with 288 GB of capacity and 18 TB/s bandwidth per chip. Microsoft claims the Maia 300 delivers 40% more tokens per MW than leading GPU based systems and offers up to 7x the rack scale throughput of the Maia 200. The previous generation, Maia 200, is already active in the US, Europe, and Australia, where it provides up to 1.7x more tokens per watt for Teams and Copilot.

Today we are announcing our biggest bet yet on our own silicon.

Starting next calendar year, we will scale our Maia family to multi-gigawatt deployments, making it the primary inference system for our own product and services.

And we’re introducing Maia 300, which delivers 40% more tokens per watt compared to leading GPU-based systems.

Our goal is to build on the full-stack efficiency gains we’ve already seen, while continuing to bring the latest innovations from across the ecosystem into our fleet.

selectedTweets.text:
Memory got smoked in Seoul today. A few hours later Microsoft announced a chip with 8 stacks of HBM4 on it. The tape and the hardware are telling two different stories.

Here's the day.

Korea: KOSPI -3.65% to 6,384, fourth straight down day. SK hynix -4.52% to ₩1.6M, Samsung -4.39% to ₩250,500, per Yonhap. Blame went to the US chip selloff over the holiday, CXMT flagging a new server memory product by end of 2026, and buyback support fading at both chipmakers.

Singapore: Hock Tan said capital might be the biggest constraint now, more than chips, memory or power. His line: "Memory shortage today might not be that way a year from now." He also said there's more demand for compute than the industry can supply, possibly through 2029 and into 2030 (per CNBC).

Then Microsoft dropped Maia 300:
- 8 HBM4 stacks, 288 GB, 18 TB/s per chip
- 96 chips per rack, 27.6 TB of HBM per rack
- Compute dies on TSMC N2P
- Reuters says Microsoft plans to deploy potentially more than a million of them next year

Quick math. If they actually get to 1M chips, that's 8M HBM4 stacks and ~288 PB of HBM. For one company's in-house inference chip. On top of Nvidia, TPUs, Trainium and OpenAI's own silicon.

This morning I said memory cycles die when everyone builds at once, not when demand dries up. Today fits that. The worry isn't today's demand. It's the supply coming: CXMT, new fabs, and now Hock saying the shortage may ease.

So the question isn't whether AI needs more HBM. It does. It's whether supply catches up faster than demand. TSMC and ASML report this week, SK hynix on Oct 27. That's where we find out.
